extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, third‑party requesters, and patent practitioners handling inter partes reexamination appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for filing, formatting, and responding to appellant and respondent briefs, cross-appeals, examiner answers, and related actions in inter partes reexamination appeals under the MPEP and 37 CFR part 41.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross‑appeal timing and limitations (37 CFR 41.61(b),(e),(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within fourteen days of service of an opposing party’s notice of appeal, a patent owner or third party requester who has not filed a notice of appeal may file a notice of cross appeal. The time for filing the notice of cross appeal may not be extended. Where the notice of cross appeal is timely filed but defective (e.g., missing fee, missing proof of service, unsigned, failure to identify appealed claims), 37 CFR 41.61(f) provides one opportunity to file, within a non‑extendable period of one month, an amended cross appeal correcting the defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross appeals are only permitted from a "notice of appeal," not from a "notice of cross appeal." If multiple requesters are present, cross appeal timing runs from the earlier applicable appeal as specified. If a cross appeal is untimely or the original appeal period expired, the later requester may be unable to appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant’s brief filing deadline (37 CFR 41.66(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant’s brief must be filed no later than two months from the latest filing date of the last‑filed notice of appeal or cross appeal, or, when a party entitled to file a notice of appeal fails to do so, no later than two months from the expiration of the time for filing such notice by the last party entitled to do so. The time for filing an appellant’s brief or an amended appellant’s brief may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each party that filed a timely and proper notice of appeal or cross appeal must file its appellant brief with fee by the later of (A) within two months from the date of the last‑filed notice of appeal or cross appeal; or (B) until expiration of time for filing by the last party entitled to do so. Late briefs risk dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant’s brief: signature and fee (37 CFR 41.67(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must be signed by the appellant or the appellant’s duly authorized attorney or agent and must be accompanied by the requisite fee set forth in § 41.20(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file a brief with the required signature and fee within the time allowed causes the appellant’s appeal to stand dismissed. The CRU/filing procedures require indicating CRU Art Unit and reexamination control number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant’s brief: required content and order (37 CFR 41.67(c)(1)(i)–(xi))
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant’s brief shall contain the following items under appropriate headings and in the order indicated: (i) Real party in interest; (ii) Related appeals and interferences; (iii) Status of claims; (iv) Status of amendments; (v) Summary of claimed subject matter (including identification of every means‑plus‑function and step‑plus‑function and corresponding specification/drawing references); (vi) Issues to be reviewed on appeal; (vii) Argument (contentions with citations, separate heading per issue, grouping/waiver rules); (viii) Claims appendix; (ix) Evidence appendix; (x) Related proceedings appendix; (xi) Certificate of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each issue must be treated under a separate heading. For patent owner appellants, identify rejected claims being appealed; for requester appellants, identify claims with favorable determinations being appealed. Copies of decisions in related proceedings must be included in the appendix. A statement that merely points out what a claim recites will not be considered an argument for separate patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument limits and format (appellant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument must set forth contentions with basis and citations of statutes, regulations, authorities, and parts of the record relied on. Any arguments or authorities not included in the brief (or briefs permitted under §§ 41.68 and 41.71) will be refused consideration unless good cause is shown. Claims may be argued separately or as a group; failure to separately argue grouped claims constitutes waiver of separate patentability argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple claims subject to the same ground are argued as a group, the Board may decide the group on a single selected claim. Each claim argued separately should be under a subheading identifying the claim; grouped claims should be under a subheading identifying the group. Oral argument will not remedy deficiencies in the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new/unentered matter in appellant brief (37 CFR 41.67(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief shall not include any new or non‑admitted amendment, or any new or non‑admitted affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.116 for amendments/affidavits filed after final action but before or on the same date as filing an appeal, and § 41.63 for amendments/affidavits/evidence after filing the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑compliant appellant brief: notification and cure period (37 CFR 41.67(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brief does not comply with all requirements of 41.67(a) and (c), appellant will be notified of reasons for non‑compliance and given a non‑extendable time period (one month) to file an amended brief. Failure to file an amended brief within the set time period, or filing one that does not overcome all reasons for non‑compliance, results in dismissal of the appellant’s appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If defect(s) not corrected, the appeal stands dismissed. If a brief is late or an amended brief is not submitted after a requirement, respondent briefs may be placed in the file but marked "not entered" and not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim copy formatting requirements in appellant brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The copy of the claims to be reviewed on appeal required in the claims appendix should be a clean copy that includes all brackets and underlining as required by 37 CFR 1.530(d) et seq.; the copy must include all underlining and bracketing necessary to reflect changes made to the original patent claims throughout prosecution. Any new claims added in the reexamination must be completely underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For convenience, the copy of the claims should start on a new page and be double spaced. Failure to comply with claim formatting may be treated as a defect in the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments, affidavits, declarations, exhibits after appeal filing (37 CFR 41.63)
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) Amendments filed after filing an appeal cancelling claims may be admitted where such cancellation does not affect scope of any other pending claim; (B) All other amendments filed after filing an appeal will not be admitted except where patent owner reopens prosecution under 37 CFR 41.77(b)(1); (C) Affidavits or other evidence filed after filing an appeal will not be admitted except where prosecution is reopened under 37 CFR 41.77(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner wants the patent owner to provide an amendment or evidence during appeal stage, the examiner must reopen prosecution, accept the amendment/evidence for entry, permit timely comment by third party requester, and then issue a new Action Closing Prosecution (ACP). See MPEP § 2673.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent’s brief filing deadline and extension prohibition (37 CFR 41.66(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an appellant’s brief has been properly filed, any respondent brief must be filed within one month from the date of service of the appellant’s brief. The time for filing a respondent’s brief or an amended respondent’s brief may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fee per 37 CFR 41.20(b)(2) is required when the respondent brief is filed for the first time in a particular reexamination proceeding. If respondent brief is late the brief will be placed in the file but marked "not entered" and not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent’s brief: limitation to issues raised (37 CFR 41.68(a)(3) & (4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent brief shall be limited to issues raised in the appellant brief to which the respondent brief is directed. A requester’s respondent brief may not address any brief of any other requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent may not propose a new ground of rejection. Where a party failed to file a timely notice of appeal or cross appeal, that party may still file a respondent brief in accordance with 37 CFR 41.66(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent’s brief: required content and specificity (37 CFR 41.68(b)(1)(i)–(x))
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent brief shall contain, under appropriate headings and in order: (i) Real party in interest; (ii) Related appeals and interferences; (iii) Status of claims (accept or dispute appellant’s statement, specifying errors with particularity if disputed); (iv) Status of amendments (accept/dispute with particularity if disputed); (v) Summary of claimed subject matter (accept/dispute with particularity if disputed); (vi) Issues to be reviewed on appeal (accept/dispute; may provide counter statement); (vii) Argument (accept/dispute appellant’s contentions, specify errors and bases with citations; each issue under separate heading); (viii) Evidence appendix; (ix) Related proceedings appendix; (x) Certificate of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If respondent disputes appellant’s statements, the respondent must specify errors with particularity. The respondent may make counter‑stated issues and must treat each under separate headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new/unentered matter in respondent brief (37 CFR 41.68(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent brief shall not include any new or non‑admitted amendment, or any new or non‑admitted affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.116 and § 41.63 for treatment of such material filed after final action or after the date of filing the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑compliant respondent brief: notification and cure (37 CFR 41.68(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a respondent brief does not comply with all requirements of 41.68(a) and (b), respondent will be notified of reasons for non‑compliance and given a non‑extendable one‑month period to file an amended brief. Failure to timely file an amended respondent brief that overcomes the reasons will result in the respondent brief and any amended respondent brief by that respondent not being considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If respondent does not file the amended brief in time, the brief will be placed in the file but marked "not entered" and not considered. If timely amended brief overcomes defects it will be entered and considered along with the original brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling informalities in one or more briefs (forms and notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an appellant or respondent brief does not comply with requirements (e.g., missing fee or portion of fee, missing signature, inappropriate signature, fewer than three copies, no proof of service), the appropriate party should be notified of reasons for non‑compliance and provided a non‑extendable one‑month period to file an amended brief. Form PTOL‑2067 is used as the cover sheet for the notification action; specific form paragraphs (e.g., ¶26.09, ¶26.10, ¶26.11) should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate PTOL‑2067 will be sent to each party where multiple briefs are non‑compliant. If the same party’s appellant and respondent briefs are both informal, examiner may combine notifications. Consequences: failure to timely file amended appellant brief leads to dismissal; failure by respondent leads to brief not being considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal conference process and examiner preparation (MPEP §2676 / §1208 procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: All appellant and respondent briefs are processed in the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU). The CRU forwards the file to the examiner after all briefs are filed or time for filing has expired. Examiner will consult with the Reexamination Legal Advisor (RLA) and formulate an initial opinion whether to prepare an examiner’s answer or reopen prosecution. If preparing an examiner’s answer, the examiner arranges an appeal conference under MPEP §1208, the RLA attends, and the examiner has two weeks following the appeal conference to prepare the examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner concludes the appeal should not go forward, prosecution is reopened and a new non‑final Office action issued; examiner should consult RLA on timing for reopening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer limits and content (37 CFR 41.69)
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner may furnish a written answer to appellant/respondent briefs explaining the invention, references relied upon, grounds of rejection, and reasons for patentability, including grounds for not adopting any proposed rejection; a copy shall be supplied to owner and all requesters. An examiner’s answer may not include a new ground of rejection or a new determination not to make a proposed rejection. Any new ground of rejection or new determination must be made in an Office action reopening prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the primary examiner determines the appeal does not comply with applicable provisions or is not an appealable action, the examiner shall make such determination of record.
